scenes.line1: Why does JVM split memory into generations?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why the JVM splits memory into generations? Let’s see how it boosts performance.

scenes.label: Generational
scenes.sub: Young gen for short-lived objects, Old gen for long-lived.
scenes.say: The heap is split into Young and Old generations. Most objects die young, so the JVM collects them more often.
G1 splits the heap into regions and aims for predictable pause times. ZGC focuses on low latency and does most work while your app runs.
Parallel GC uses several threads to collect the Young generation fast. It’s great when you need raw throughput, like in batch jobs.

scenes.question: Which GC is always best for low latency?
scenes.right: ZGC or G1 are better for low latency apps; Parallel GC prioritizes throughput.
scenes.say: Don’t just pick Parallel GC for everything. For low-latency services, ZGC or G1 are usually better choices.
